prompt: What is the slope of a line perpendicular to the graph of $y = \tfrac{3}{4}x - 2$?
hint: Perpendicular slopes are negative reciprocals — you must both flip and negate.

hints.text: Perpendicular slopes are negative reciprocals — you must both flip and negate.
Flip $\tfrac{3}{4}$ to get $\tfrac{4}{3}$, then attach the opposite sign.

learningObjective: Apply the negative-reciprocal condition for perpendicular lines.
explanation: The given slope is $\tfrac{3}{4}$, so the perpendicular slope $m$ satisfies $\tfrac{3}{4}m = -1$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Why both wrong answers exist
steps: Choice B negated but forgot to flip; choice C flipped but forgot to negate.
The College Board builds one distractor for each half of the rule, every single time.
Say the rule as two separate actions — "flip it, then negate it" — and check that you performed both.
